Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Mr. Mohd. Azim, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. Digvijay Nath Dubey and Mr. Jagdish
Singh Bisht, Advocates for the respondent.
2. Supplementary counter affidavit filed by
respondent in Court today is taken on record.
Petitioner participated in a selection for the post
of Assistant Executive in Indian Institute of
Management, Kashipur. As per the
advertisement dated 26.09.2022, candidates
claiming benefit of reservation available to
Other Backward Classes, were required to
submit OBC certificate issued by competent
authority in the prescribed format.
3. Since petitioner's name did not figure in
the final list of shortlisted candidates, therefore,
she approached this Court, seeking the
following reliefs:
"(i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of Certiorari quashing the impugned Final
List of Shortlisted candidates for the post of
Assistant Executive (Annexure-6) so far it does not
include the name of the petitioner.
(ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of Mandamus commanding and directing the
respondents to include the name of petitioner in
Final List of Shortlisted candidates for the post of
Assistant Executive and to permit her in appearing
in the written examination."

2026:UHC:1633
4. Learned counsel appearing for respondent
submits that petitioner had not submitted OBC
certificate in the prescribed format; he submits
that every candidate claiming reservation
available to OBC category had to submit a
certificate that he does not fall in the creamy
layer, however petitioner failed to meet that
requirement, therefore, her name was not
included in the final list of shortlisted
candidates.
5. Learned counsel for respondent submits
that Annexure SA-1 to the supplementary
affidavit, filed by petitioner was issued on
27.06.2024 which is after the last date of
submission of application, pursuant to
advertisement issued on 26.09.2022.
6. This Court finds substance in the said
submission. Since the caste certificate produced
by petitioner was not in the prescribed format,
therefore, petitioner's application was liable to
be rejected in view of the specific condition
mentioned in the advertisement.
7. Thus there is no scope for interference in
the matter. Writ petition fails and is dismissed.
(Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
